questions.prompt: Why does Pull start with developer environment and Git before protocol lessons?

options.label: Bitcoin contributions ship as reviewed code, not solo experiments
Git replaces the need to run a node
Open source projects never use branches
Cryptography is optional for wallet engineers

questions.explanation: The foundations section builds the toolchain and collaboration habits you need before touching consensus code.

questions.prompt: What property makes a cryptographic hash useful in Bitcoin?

options.label: Hashes can be reversed to recover the preimage
Small input changes produce unpredictable output changes
Two different inputs always share the same digest
Hashes encrypt private keys for storage

questions.explanation: One-way hashes commit to data; tiny changes avalanche into totally different digests.

questions.prompt: What does a digital signature prove in a Bitcoin transaction?

options.label: The transaction will confirm in the next block
The recipient's identity was verified off-chain
The spender authorized spending those inputs
The fee rate is optimal for current mempool conditions

questions.explanation: Signatures prove authorization; anyone can verify them with the public key without seeing the private key.

questions.prompt: Approximately how often does the Bitcoin block subsidy halve?

options.label: Every 1,000 blocks
Whenever fees exceed the subsidy
Never; the subsidy is fixed forever
Every ~210,000 blocks (~4 years)

questions.explanation: Halvings follow the 210,000-block schedule defined in consensus rules.

questions.prompt: When block space is congested, what usually happens to confirmation times for low-fee transactions?

options.label: They wait longer because miners prioritize higher fee rates
They confirm faster because the network speeds up
Fees are ignored; transactions confirm in arrival order
The subsidy automatically pays their fees

questions.explanation: Block space is scarce; users bid with fees and miners select profitable transactions.

questions.prompt: How does the UTXO model differ from an account-balance ledger?

options.label: Each address has a running balance stored on-chain
Wallets track discrete outputs that are fully consumed when spent
UTXOs can be partially debited like a bank account
Only miners hold UTXOs; users hold accounts

questions.explanation: Spending consumes whole UTXOs; change is returned as new outputs.

questions.prompt: What does SegWit move into the witness portion of a transaction?

options.label: The block subsidy amount
Private keys for faster signing
Signature and script data, counted with discounted weight
Mempool policy rules

questions.explanation: SegWit separates witness data and uses weight units (vbytes) for block limits.

questions.prompt: What is the typical privacy advantage of a Taproot key-path spend?

options.label: It hides the transaction from the mempool entirely
It removes the need for signatures
It encrypts the recipient address
On-chain it looks like a simple single-sig spend

questions.explanation: Alternative script paths stay hidden unless a script-path spend is used.

questions.prompt: How is a transaction fee calculated at the consensus level?

options.label: Sum of input values minus sum of output values
A fixed fee field set by the recipient
10 satoshis per byte regardless of inputs
The miner subsidy plus a protocol tax

questions.explanation: There is no explicit fee output; the difference between inputs and outputs is the fee.

questions.prompt: What does Replace-by-Fee (BIP-125) allow a wallet to do?

options.label: Refund confirmed transactions after six blocks
Replace an unconfirmed tx with a higher-fee version when signaled
Change the recipient of a confirmed payment
Bypass proof-of-work for urgent sends

questions.explanation: RBF lets users bump fees on stuck unconfirmed transactions that opted in.

questions.prompt: What is the main role of Bitcoin's P2P network?

options.label: Store user account balances centrally
Issue new bitcoin to wallets on demand
Gossip valid transactions and blocks between peers
Replace the need for local validation

questions.explanation: Nodes validate first, then relay; there is no central Bitcoin server.

questions.prompt: Why is eclipse resistance important for a full node?

options.label: It only affects mining pools, not wallets
Eclipse attacks steal private keys from disk
More peers always means weaker security
An attacker controlling your peers can feed you a fake chain tip

questions.explanation: If you only talk to adversarial peers, you may accept invalid or minority-chain data.

questions.prompt: How does an SPV light client differ from a fully validating node?

options.label: It trusts block headers and Merkle proofs instead of verifying every script
It mines blocks without a full chain download
It stores the entire UTXO set in browser localStorage
It cannot detect payments at all

questions.explanation: SPV clients trade bandwidth for trust assumptions about miners and peers.

questions.prompt: What defines a soft fork compared to a hard fork?

options.label: Soft forks delete all historical transactions
Soft forks tighten rules; old nodes still see valid blocks
Hard forks never require coordination
Only soft forks change proof-of-work

questions.explanation: Soft forks make previously valid blocks/transactions invalid under new rules while remaining backward compatible at the block level.

questions.prompt: What does proof-of-work primarily secure in Bitcoin?

options.label: Encryption of wallet seeds
Instant finality of unconfirmed payments
Ordering and immutability of the heaviest valid chain
Privacy of sender IP addresses

questions.explanation: Work makes rewriting recent history expensive; difficulty adjusts to target block intervals.

questions.prompt: What problem do output descriptors (BIP-380 family) solve for wallet engineers?

options.label: Replace the need for private keys
Store mempool transactions in SQL
Mine blocks from a browser tab
Express spending policies in a portable, machine-readable form

questions.explanation: Descriptors document how keys and scripts map to addresses for backup and signing workflows.

questions.prompt: What does BIP-32 enable in an HD wallet?

options.label: Deriving many keys from one seed with a structured path
Storing bitcoin without any keys
Automatic fee negotiation with miners
On-chain encrypted messaging

questions.explanation: Hierarchical deterministic derivation lets one backup regenerate many addresses.

questions.prompt: Why is regtest preferred for integration tests over mainnet?

options.label: Regtest uses real money for realistic UX
You control block production and coin supply locally
Mainnet cannot broadcast transactions
Regtest skips script validation

questions.explanation: Regtest lets you mine instantly and reset state without financial risk.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of PSBT (BIP-174)?

options.label: Publish blocks to the P2P network
Encode Lightning invoices
Pass partially built transactions between signers and devices
Replace the UTXO set with accounts

questions.explanation: PSBT standardizes multi-party signing across software, hardware, and coordinators.

questions.prompt: What is a critical security rule when exposing Bitcoin Core RPC?

options.label: Bind RPC to 0.0.0.0 without a password for convenience
Share cookie auth in public GitHub issues
Disable TLS because localhost is always safe
Never expose it publicly; authenticate and firewall it

questions.explanation: RPC can move funds and control the node; treat it like root access.

questions.prompt: What should a mini-wallet project demonstrate on regtest?

options.label: Generate addresses, receive funds, and send with correct change
Rewrite Bitcoin Core consensus rules
Store seeds in the README for reproducibility
Skip transaction broadcasting entirely

questions.explanation: The mini-wallet ties together keys, UTXOs, fees, and broadcasting on a private chain.

questions.prompt: What does BIP-21 standardize for merchants?

options.label: Lightning routing hints in invoices
A URI scheme for payment requests (bitcoin:...)
Hardware wallet firmware updates
Mempool eviction policy

questions.explanation: BIP-21 links amount, address, and labels into scannable payment URIs.

questions.prompt: When building a block explorer UI, what is a common data source pattern?

options.label: Scrape social media for balances
Ask users to email their xpub
Index chain data from your own node or Esplora-style API
Hard-code mainnet balances for demo speed

questions.explanation: Explorers visualize data your backend indexes from validated chain sources.

questions.prompt: What should payment-processor webhooks include for merchant trust?

options.label: Private keys for automatic sweeping
Unauthenticated GET callbacks only
Marketing copy instead of txids
Signed payloads and clear confirmation thresholds

questions.explanation: Merchants need verifiable events tied to on-chain confirmation depth.

questions.prompt: Which environment is preferred for Bitcoin project demos on Pull?

options.label: Regtest or Polar over mainnet for learning
Mainnet with real funds for every exercise
Mocked JSON with no node
Production merchant traffic only

questions.explanation: Local labs are safer and faster for iteration; document how to reproduce.

questions.prompt: Before opening a Bitcoin OSS pull request, you should:

options.label: Open a large refactor without maintainer discussion
Read CONTRIBUTING, find agreed scope, and run relevant tests
Skip CI because Bitcoin is decentralized
Copy code without attribution

questions.explanation: Maintainers expect scoped changes, tests, and alignment with project norms.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the meaningful-PR rubric?

options.label: Replace all code review
Score quiz answers only
Self-check problem fit, scope, correctness, and communication before shipping
Guarantee automatic merge

questions.explanation: The rubric helps you judge whether a PR is worth a maintainer's time.

questions.prompt: What makes a builder portfolio credible to maintainers?

options.label: Buzzwords without links to code
Private gists only
Screenshots of other people's work
Verifiable repos, commits, PRs, and concise writeups

questions.explanation: Evidence beats adjectives; link what you built and what was merged.

questions.prompt: During maintainer feedback cycles, you should:

options.label: Address review comments, keep scope tight, and re-run tests
Force-push without reading feedback
Open a new PR for every typo fix
Argue that tests are optional for docs changes

questions.explanation: Iteration is normal; responsive, tested updates build trust.

questions.prompt: When triaging good first issues, prioritize:

options.label: Issues labeled 'rewrite everything'
Clear reproduction, maintainer interest, and a bounded fix
Closed issues from five years ago
Features no maintainer asked for

questions.explanation: Scoped issues with maintainer buy-in are the fastest path to a merged PR.
